title: Terms of service
intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Barmajiyat Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales [TODO(MUT-732): company number and registered office] ("we", "us"), which owns MTB3A, for using MTB3A: its website, its web portal and its iPhone and Android apps. By creating an account or using MTB3A, you accept these terms and our privacy policy, which is part of them. If you don't accept them, please don't use MTB3A. These terms apply equally to everyone, whatever their gender.

sections.title: 1. The service
body: MTB3A helps freelancers and small businesses record what they earn, what they're owed, what they've been paid and what they spend, in each currency, across their personal money and the businesses they run. With an account, your records are kept on our servers, behind your sign-in, so every device you sign in on shows the same numbers. Where it is turned on for your business profile, MTB3A can also issue Israeli tax documents, as section 6 describes.

You can also try the web portal without an account. Your records then stay in your browser on that device and never reach our servers; these terms apply to that use too, apart from what they say about accounts, fees and our servers.
We may improve, change or remove features. If a change takes away something you rely on, we'll tell you in advance.

sections.title: 2. Who may use MTB3A
body: You must be at least 18 years old and able to make a binding agreement. When you accept these terms for a business profile you own, you confirm that you may agree to them on that business's behalf. People you share a profile with accept these terms for themselves.

sections.title: 3. Your account
body: You create your account yourself on the web portal, or we set it up for you; either way, you choose your password through a link we email you. Give us correct details and keep them up to date.

Keep your password, passkeys and two-step sign-in codes to yourself: you are responsible for what is done with your account. If you think someone else has used it, tell us straight away. Before you issue tax documents or connect a profile to the Israel Tax Authority, we may require you to turn on two-step sign-in.

sections.title: 4. Plans, trial, fees and payment
body: Every account can use the free Starter plan: one business beside your personal profile, 3 issued documents and 12 receipt scans a month, without the Tax Authority connection. Our paid plans, Solo, Business and Firm, raise these limits and include the Tax Authority connection; each plan's limits are shown when you subscribe. A new account may be offered, once, a 14-day trial of the Solo plan, with a card: nothing is charged before the trial ends, and you can cancel any time before then. If you don't cancel, your Solo subscription starts when the trial ends and renews as described below; if you cancel, your account moves to Starter. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q7): the notice and consent a trial that renews into a paid plan needs.]

The price is the one shown when you subscribe, or the one in the offer we sent you. Prices are shown before VAT. If your billing address is in Israel, we add Israeli VAT (currently 18%); elsewhere, we add any tax the law of your country requires. The country of the billing address you give when you subscribe also sets the currency you pay in. You pay monthly or yearly in advance, by card through Stripe, our payment provider, and your subscription renews for the same period until you cancel it. Before a price change for your plan takes effect, we'll tell you in advance, and you can cancel before then. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q6): whether prices shown to consumers in Israel must include VAT; the notice period for a price change.]

If a payment fails and stays unpaid after we have reminded you, your plan ends and your account moves to the free Starter plan. Businesses beyond Starter's limits stay available to read and download. We never delete your records because a payment lapsed.

sections.title: 5. Cancelling and refunds
body: You can cancel your subscription at any time in the web portal (Billing › Cancel plan), or by writing to info@mtb3a.com. Cancelling stops the next renewal. You keep full use of MTB3A until the end of the period you have paid for; after that, your account becomes read-only and your records stay available to read and download, until you subscribe again or continue free on the Starter plan.

If you are a consumer, you may also cancel in any way the Consumer Protection Law, 5741-1981, allows. You may cancel a new subscription within 14 days of the transaction and get your money back, less any cancellation fee the law permits, but only if you have not used MTB3A since you subscribed: once you have added or changed records, issued a document or downloaded your data under the subscription, the service has been supplied to you and this 14-day right no longer applies. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q5): confirm that using the service ends the 14-day right, and this wording.] During the free trial nothing is charged: your paid subscription starts only after the 14-day trial, so cancelling during the trial costs nothing.
Fees for a period that has already started are not refunded, except where the law requires a refund, which we will then make.

sections.title: 6. Issuing tax documents
body: Where issuing is turned on for your business profile, you can issue tax invoices, tax invoice-receipts, receipts and credit notes, and payment requests, which are not tax documents. MTB3A produces each document from the details you enter, numbers it in sequence for its type, and signs its PDF electronically.

You are responsible for every document you issue: that your business details and your client's, the lines, amounts, VAT, dates and the type of document are correct and complete; that you issue it on time and as the law requires; that you report it to the tax authorities and record it in your own books; and that you check it before you send it. An issued document can't be edited or deleted: a mistake is corrected with a credit note or a new document, as the bookkeeping rules require.

Some tax invoices need an allocation number from the Israel Tax Authority before your client may deduct their VAT. To get one through MTB3A, you connect your business profile to the Tax Authority yourself, with your own sign-in there, and you authorize us to ask for allocation numbers in your name for the invoices you issue. The connection lasts as long as the Tax Authority allows (currently 90 days), and you can disconnect at any time. The connection is included on our paid plans (Solo and above). On a plan without it you can still issue every document: you request the allocation number on the Tax Authority's site yourself and enter it. If your plan changes to one without the connection, we pause it and keep it, and it works again when you move back to a paid plan, as long as the Tax Authority's own approval hasn't ended. The Tax Authority decides whether to give a number. If its systems are unavailable, refuse or answer late, we can't give you one, but you may enter a number you obtained from the Tax Authority yourself. We are not responsible for the Tax Authority's decisions or the availability of its systems.

The Tax Authority connection is for your own profile's documents. Don't pass it on, lend it, resell it, or let anyone outside your profile use it. An accountant you have shared your profile with works inside your profile, which is allowed. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q8): confirm this wording.]

MTB3A is being registered with the Israel Tax Authority as invoicing software. Its registered software house is Narabnd Studio Ltd (נאראבנד סטודיו בע"מ), company number 517108775, Az-Zahra St. 18, Jerusalem, a related company that holds the connection to the Tax Authority and signs the documents you issue, under a licence from us. Once MTB3A is registered, its registration number will be shown here. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q3): whether Narabnd is named in these terms, and its role for issued documents (holder or processor).]

We keep the documents you issue for 7 years from each document's date, as our privacy policy describes. The legal duty to keep your books is still yours: download your documents and the uniform file, and keep your own copies.

sections.title: 7. Your records are yours
body: You own everything you enter. We use it only to run MTB3A for you, as our privacy policy describes, and we never sell it.

For the details you record about your own clients and suppliers, you decide what is recorded and why. We hold them on your behalf and act on them only to run MTB3A for you: we keep them confidential and secure, let only the people who run MTB3A reach them when needed, use only the providers our privacy policy lists, and delete them as it describes. You are responsible for having the right to record them, and for telling the people concerned where the law requires it.
You can download a copy of your records at any time from Your data, or ask us and we'll send them to you as a file.

sections.title: 8. Sharing with others
body: You choose who else sees your records: co-owners and team members of a profile, an accountant you give read access, or anyone you give a share link and its PIN. You can end their access at any time, but files they have already downloaded are their copy, and we can't recall them.
If a profile is connected to Malafat, or you connect another app to your account where MTB3A offers it, the records you allow are shared with it, and its own terms apply to what it does with them.

sections.title: 9. Using it fairly
body: Don't use MTB3A for anything illegal, including issuing false or fictitious documents. Don't try to reach anyone else's records, test or get around our security, copy, take apart or resell the service, collect data from it automatically, overload it, or upload anything harmful such as malware.

If you break these rules, we may suspend your account. We'll tell you first and give you a chance to fix it, unless we must act at once to protect the service, other people or the law. If you issued false documents or misused the Tax Authority connection, we may also disconnect it and report it where the law requires.

sections.title: 10. Our rights in MTB3A
body: MTB3A, its software, design, name and logo belong to us or to those who license them to us. While these terms apply, you may use MTB3A for yourself and your business; you get no other right in it. What you enter stays yours, and you allow us only what we need to store, process and show it to run MTB3A for you. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q2): the assignment of MTB3A's intellectual property from its developer to Barmajiyat Ltd, and Barmajiyat's licence to Narabnd, are not yet signed; sign them before publication.]

sections.title: 11. We are not your accountant
body: MTB3A records what you enter, adds it up and produces the documents you ask for. It is not accounting, tax or legal advice, and it doesn't file tax returns or reports for you. Totals, VAT figures, reports and the suggestions MTB3A makes, including the amounts, dates and vendors it reads from receipts, can be wrong. Conversion rates are for reference only.
Check important figures and every document yourself, or with your accountant, before you rely on them or send them.

sections.title: 12. Availability
body: We work to keep MTB3A available and your records safe, and we back them up every day. We can't promise the service will never be interrupted, for example during maintenance, an outage at our hosting provider, or a fault in the Tax Authority's systems. If we ever stop offering MTB3A, we'll tell you at least 60 days in advance, so you can download your records and documents.

sections.title: 13. Closing your account
body: You can close your account yourself at any time with Close my account: in the web portal under You › Account, or in the iPhone and Android apps on the Account tab. You then have 30 days to change your mind and keep it. After that we delete your account, the profiles you own with every record in them, and the record that you accepted these terms. Profiles you share with others stay with them, and what you added stays without your name. A few things are kept after that, as our privacy policy lists, among them the tax documents you issued, which are kept for 7 years from each document's date. Our backups clear 14 days after deletion.
Before you close it, download your records and your issued documents: once they are deleted, we can't get them back. Closing your account doesn't end your own duty to keep your books.

sections.title: 14. Liability
body: MTB3A is provided as it is. We are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profit or lost business; for losses caused by records or documents you entered incorrectly; or for losses caused by others, such as the Tax Authority, a payment provider or an app you connected.
Our total liability to you under these terms is limited to the fees you paid us in the 12 months before the claim.
Nothing in these terms limits liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as for fraud or wilful harm, or takes away rights you have as a consumer under the law that applies to you.

sections.title: 15. Changes to these terms
body: We may update these terms. When we do, we'll ask you to read and accept the new version, by email or the next time you open your account. Every earlier version stays available at its own address, so you can always see what you agreed to.

If you are a consumer living outside Israel, you also keep the protection of the mandatory consumer law of the country where you live, and you may bring a claim in its courts.
These terms are written in English and Arabic. If the two texts differ, the English text prevails.

sections.title: 17. General
body: If a court finds part of these terms unenforceable, the rest stays in force. If we don't enforce a right straight away, we haven't given it up. We may transfer these terms to a company that takes over MTB3A, and we'll tell you if we do; you may transfer them only with our written agreement.

sections.title: 18. Contact
body: Write to us at info@mtb3a.com. We reply within 2 working days. By post: Barmajiyat Ltd, [TODO(MUT-732): registered office].
